```json
{
  "design": "Fuzzy regression discontinuity (RD) design",
  "instrument": "Crossing the eligibility threshold (score >= 70), which sharply raises the probability of participation but does not deterministically assign it",
  "estimand": "Local average treatment effect (LATE) of program participation for compliers at the score cutoff of 70 — i.e., the effect for those whose participation status changes because of crossing the threshold",
  "global_generalization": "No. The estimate is local to the cutoff; it applies to units near the threshold (and specifically to compliers there), not automatically to everyone, including far-below-cutoff individuals or always/never-takers near the threshold.",
  "assumptions": [
    "Continuity: potential outcomes (and all confounders) vary smoothly through the score of 70 absent treatment, so units just above and just below the cutoff are comparable",
    "Exclusion restriction: the score affects employment only through program participation (no direct effect of the score or eligibility itself on outcomes)",
    "Monotonicity: crossing the cutoff can only increase (never decrease) the probability of participation — no defiers",
    "No other policy changes or treatments discontinuously at the threshold of 70",
    "The score cannot be precisely manipulated, so no sorting of units to one side of the cutoff",
    "SUTVA / no interference: one unit's participation does not affect another unit's outcomes"
  ]
}
```
message.reasoning: Sharp vs fuzzy RD: participation jumps but not universal above cutoff, some below participate → fuzzy RD. Instrument: crossing the cutoff (score ≥ 70). Estimand: LATE for compliers at the threshold (local average treatment effect at cutoff). Global generalization: no, only local to cutoff. Assumptions: continuity of potential outcomes, monotonicity, exclusion restriction (score affects outcome only through participation), no other changes at threshold, SUTVA.
